theory_refs.why: The trigger for a variable window.

theory_refs.at: If [l, r] is invalid, so is [l, r+1]
theory_refs.why: Why l never needs to move back.

theory_refs.at: Counts of characters in the window

stages.title: Understand
stages.body:
✍️ f(string) → length of the longest substring (contiguous) with all characters distinct.
- Length ≤ 5·10⁴; letters, digits, symbols, spaces.
- "abcabcbb" → 3 ("abc"). "bbbbb" → 1. "pwwkew" → 3 ("wke").

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body:
✍️ By hand on "pwwkew": I grow "pw"; the next 'w' repeats, so I drop characters from the left until the old 'w' is gone → "w"; grow "wke"; next 'w' repeats → drop "wk" … → "ew".
✍️ Hard part: knowing how far to drop from the left.
✍️ Edges: empty string → 0; all identical; spaces count as characters.

stages.title: Brainstorm: brute → optimal
stages.body:
✍️ **1. Brute.** Every substring, check distinctness with a set. O(n³) or O(n²).
✍️ ↳ Bottleneck: for each end r, retrying every start from scratch.
✍️ ↳ Observation: if [l, r] has a repeat, every longer window [l, r+1] does too. So once a start is invalid for r, it stays invalid → the best start only moves right.
✍️ **2. Optimal (window + counts).** Expand r; while the new character's count > 1, remove s[l] and l++. Record r − l + 1. O(n).
✍️ **3. Variant.** Store each character's last index and jump l to max(l, last[c] + 1) — no inner loop.

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body:
✍️ 1. Keep a count of characters in the window [l, r]; l starts at 0.
✍️ 2. For each r, add s[r] to the counts.
✍️ 3. While s[r] appears more than once, remove s[l] from the counts and move l right.
✍️ 4. The window is now valid; update the best length.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
STATE   cnt[256] = 0; l = 0; best = 0
LOOP    for r in 0..n-1
UPDATE    cnt[s[r]]++
          while cnt[s[r]] > 1:          (only s[r] can be duplicated)
              cnt[s[l]]--; l++
CHECK     best = max(best, r - l + 1)
RETURN  best
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Dry run
stages.body:
"pwwkew":
| r | s[r] | shrink? | window | best |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | p | no | p | 1 |
| 1 | w | no | pw | 2 |
| 2 | w | drop p, drop w | w | 2 |
| 3 | k | no | wk | 2 |
| 4 | e | no | wke | 3 |
| 5 | w | drop w | kew | 3 |

stages.title: Edge cases and complexity
stages.body:
✍️ O(n) time: r moves n times, l at most n times in total. O(1) space (256 counters).
✍️ Only the newly added character can create a duplicate, so the while condition checks `cnt[s[r]]`.
- Casting to `unsigned char` keeps the index non-negative for any byte.

stages.title: Carry forward
stages.body:
✍️ "Longest substring with a property that breaks by adding and heals by removing" → variable window.
✍️ Expand always; shrink while invalid; record after the shrink.
✍️ The window's state is a count table; validity is a question about it.

stages.title: Interview follow-ups
stages.body:
- *Avoid the inner loop.* last[c] = last index; l = max(l, last[c] + 1). Still O(n).
- *At most k distinct characters.* Track distinct count; shrink while distinct > k ([[sw-frequency-map-window#distinct]]).
- *Return the substring.* Remember l when best improves.

siblings.title: Fruit Into Baskets
siblings.maps: Longest window with at most 2 distinct values — the rule changes from "no repeats" to "≤ 2 kinds".

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Longest contiguous run containing at most two distinct fruit types.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Variable window with a count map and a distinct counter; shrink while distinct > 2. O(n).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Add fruit[r] (if its count was 0, distinct++); while distinct > 2 remove fruit[l] (if count becomes 0, distinct−−); record.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
for r: if cnt[f[r]]++ == 0: d++
    while d > 2: if --cnt[f[l]] == 0: d--; l++
    best = max(best, r-l+1)
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ "At most k distinct" → distinct counter updated on 0↔1 transitions ([[sw-frequency-map-window#distinct]]).

siblings.title: Minimum Window Substring
siblings.maps: Shortest window that contains every character of t (with counts) — the "shortest valid" skeleton.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Smallest substring of s containing all characters of t, including duplicates; "" if none.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ need[c] = count in t; missing = |t|. Expand r: if need[s[r]] > 0 then missing−−; need[s[r]]−−. While missing == 0 (valid): record, then remove s[l] (need++, if it becomes > 0 missing++), l++. O(n + m).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Expand until all characters are covered; then shrink as long as it stays covered, recording the shortest.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
need from t; missing = |t|
for r: if need[s[r]]-- > 0: missing--
    while missing == 0:
        record window; if ++need[s[l]] > 0: missing++; l++
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body:
✍️ Shortest valid: shrink **while valid**, record **inside** the loop ([[sw-variable-window#template-shortest]]).
✍️ `need` going negative just means "more than required in the window" — that is fine.

siblings.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
siblings.maps: Shortest window with sum ≥ target; positive values make the sum monotone.

stages.title: Analyse
stages.body: ✍️ Minimal length of a subarray with sum ≥ target (all values positive); 0 if none.

stages.title: Brainstorm
stages.body: ✍️ Positive values → growing the window increases the sum, shrinking decreases it → monotone → shortest-valid window. O(n).

stages.title: Algorithm in words
stages.body: ✍️ Add a[r]; while sum ≥ target: record length, remove a[l], l++.

stages.title: Pseudocode
stages.body:
```
for r: sum += a[r]
    while sum >= target: best = min(best, r-l+1); sum -= a[l++]
return best == INF ? 0 : best
```

stages.title: Reference Java
Quick theory
stages.body: ✍️ This only works because values are positive ([[sw-monotonicity-requirement#rule]]).
